feedback: Approved for the race. The candidate keeps the iteration 1 base (base_speed 1.3, ki 0.02, last_direction, weights [-1,-0.5,0,0.5,1]) and changes only the sensing and gain levers that the earlier evidence points to. Iteration 1 finished 18 of 20 oval trials at mean time 1.89 s, so base_speed 1.3 is fast enough and should not be changed yet. Both iteration 1 failures were off-track exits on the s-bend (progress 0.27) and slalom (progress 0.18), with max_error about 0.062 to 0.063 m. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), which is 0.06 m for this body width, so the wider body gives no extra margin. The five sensors in iteration 1 span only ±0.04 m, so the tape can slide out of view on sharp bends, which supports widening the span. Iteration 0 also showed max_error near 0.06 m at higher gain, so gain alone is unlikely to solve it. The candidate's rationale also cites a 0.0525 m limit in places; the correct limit is 0.06 m, and the candidate should not rely on that margin. Next race: if s-bend and slalom still end off-track with max_error at or above 0.06 m, widen the span further only if sensor_size and geometry allow, or lower kp toward 2.5 while keeping kd at 1.0. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.3 (iteration 1 oval was 0.23), raise kd further before raising kp. If oval completion drops below the iteration 1 level (0.9), revert sensor_size to 0.012 to test whether the larger footprint is causing the problem.
requested_changes: If s-bend or slalom still end off_track with max_error at or above 0.06 m: keep the ±0.06 m sensor span, and lower kp from 3.0 toward 2.5 to test whether the steering is overshooting the bend.
If steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.3 on any track (iteration 1 oval baseline 0.23): raise kd from 1.0 to about 1.3 before changing kp again.
If oval completion falls below the iteration 1 level (18 of 20): revert sensor_size from 0.016 to 0.012 while keeping the wider span, to isolate whether the larger footprint is the cause.
